news.title: World Cup winner sent off 43 seconds into debut without even touching the ball and left in complete disbelief
news.lede: DJIBRIL SIDIBE’S nightmare Le Mans debut could hardly have started any worse. The 2018 World Cup winner was sent off just 43 SECONDS after coming off the bench – without even touching the ball. Sidibe joined Le Mans this summer after leaving Toulouse, but his first appearance for the club turned into a horror show. The 34-year-old had barely entered the action when he caught Esteban Lepaul on the ankle with a nasty challenge.

news.title: Lionel Messi’s greatest trophy is not the World Cup
news.lede: Lionel Messi’s Barcelona story famously began with an agreement written on a napkin.More than 25 years later, one of the biggest chapters of his football story has ended with another handwritten piece of paper.Messi announced his retirement from international football with a handwritten note shared on social media.For people who could not read Spanish, the meaning was not immediately clear. But once the translations started appearing, they realised they were reading a poignant farewell message from the greatest player of our generation.And it hurt.One sentence read: “I gave everything, I have nothing left to give.” You did give everything.And then came the note at the very end.“. I wrote these words on July 21, two days after the final.

news.title: Lionel Messi retires from international football - here's why he's the GOAT
news.lede: Superstar striker Lionel Messi has announced he is retiring from international football after more than 20 years playing for Argentina. This means he will still play for his club, Inter Miami, but will not play for his country or take part in international tournaments. The 39-year-old captained Argentina when they won the World Cup in 2022, and led the team to the final again this summer, where they lost to Spain. In a statement on social media, he said it was a decision that "hurt" but that "the time has come".

news.title: Messi retirement: FIFA president, Angel Di Maria pay glowing tribute to the GOAT
news.lede: Lionel Messi on Monday (August 31, 2026) announced his retirement from international football, leading to an outpouring of tribute and farewell messages to the football legend who is often called the GOAT (Greatest of All Time). The 39-year-old Argentina footballer, who captained his team to World Cup glory in 2022 and ‌another final in 2026, made the announcement on Instagram, describing it as “a decision that hurts the soul.” FIFA president Gianni Infantino and fellow Argentinian players are among those who have dedicated glowing tributes to the sporting icon. Here’s a look at the reactions to Messi’s retirement:.

news.title: Lionel Messi by the numbers: Trophies, heartache and the greatest World Cup player in history
news.lede: Argentina captain Lionel Messi officially brought down the curtain on a glittering 21-year international career on Monday. Messi guided Argentina to the 2026 World Cup final this summer, scoring eight goals along the way, but they fell to Spain in the championship match. The 39-year-old said the loss to Spain, coupled with his father's recent death, left him "convinced" the time was right to call time on his Argentina career. “After all this time since the final, and after thinking about it a lot, I want to tell everyone that I’m retiring from the national team.

news.title: Did You Know Lionel Messi Quit International Football in 2016? His Comeback Was Legendary
news.lede: After 21 years of representing Argentina at the highest level, Lionel Messi has called time on his international career. At 39, this pretty much is a done deal, and no more surprises are expected. Because this is actually not the first time that Messi announced his international retirement. The previous occasion that such a thing happened was 10 years ago.

news.title: From Rosario to retiring at 39: Lionel Messi was signed at 13 on a napkin; at 29, he almost quit football
news.lede: For more than two decades, Lionel Messi was not merely the name of just another footballer; he was a moving argument for persistence with discipline. The boy from Rosario who left Argentina at 13 to pursue a dream in Barcelona grew into one of the most decorated players the game has ever produced.On August 31, 2026, Messi finally stopped the clock on that dream that became an illustrious journey. Per Reuters, the 39-year-old announced his retirement from international football, ending a 21-year senior career with Argentina. His final appearance was in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, where Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time.As it stands now, Messi leaves the national team with 125 goals in 207 appearances, two Copa América titles, and the World Cup trophy he had spent much of his career chasing.However, it’s important to note that this is not retirement from football altogether.
